## Module overview

We begin exploring the research article. You learn about the authors, background on malaria and *Delftia tsuruhatensis*, and how the study was developed to address the research questions.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this module, you should be able to:

- Explain the introduction of the article in 3-5 sentences.
- Identify the research question/goal the researchers had.
- Summarize the methods and findings identified in the introduction.

```{ojs}
checklist("module-2-todo", ["Review the Delftia background before the first session", "Complete the in-class activity and submit individually", "Create a representation (flow chart? terminology list?) of the introduction and background"])
```

## Why this article?

The paper, published in *Science* in 2023, describes a naturally occurring, non-genetically modified symbiotic bacterium, *D. tsuruhatensis* TC1, isolated from mosquitoes unable to sustain *Plasmodium falciparum* development.

## Read the title in pieces

Break the title into parts: organism, relationship, effect, and host.

<details><summary>Hint: Organism, relationship, effect, host</summary>
Look for the bacterium's name, the word describing how it lives with its host, what it does to the parasite, and the insect it lives in.
</details>

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
quiz("m2q1", "In the title, 'symbiont' means TC1 is…", ["A parasite of humans", "A microbe living in association with the mosquito", "A drug", "A virus"], 1, "A symbiont lives in association with a host.")
```


```{ojs}
//| echo: false
quiz("m2q2", "What makes D. tsuruhatensis TC1 notable in this article?", ["It is genetically modified", "It is a naturally occurring symbiont linked to blocking Plasmodium development", "It causes malaria", "It was isolated from soil in Delft"], 1, "TC1 is a natural, non-modified symbiont from mosquitoes.")
```

::: {.takeaways}
### Key takeaways
- The introduction frames the problem (malaria), the approach (a symbiont) and the research question.
- TC1 is naturally occurring and not genetically modified.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Article: Huang et al. (2023), *Delftia tsuruhatensis* TC1 symbiont suppresses malaria transmission by anopheline mosquitoes, *Science*. <https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adf8141>
:::
